description.value: The study tested whether pretreatment neural reactivity to smoking cues in five a priori limbic/paralimbic regions predicted duration to first smoking lapse during smoking cessation treatment.

spans.text: This study examined whether pretreatment brain reactivity to smoking cues predicted duration to first lapse in smoking cessation treatment.

value: We hypothesized that the five regions identified by Kuhn and Gallinat would be most associated with cue-reactivity across all substances (right and left ventral striatum, caudal and rostral anterior cingulate cortex, and amygdala) would significantly be associated with the duration participants remained abstinent after cessation in an organized smoking cessation program.

description.value: A block-design smoking cue-reactivity paradigm in which participants viewed smoking images, neutral images, rest fixation, and craving rating screens across two imaging runs.

instructions.value: Participants were instructed to pay attention to the photographs and, when prompted, rate their craving for cigarettes from 0 to 8 using an MRI-compatible button box.

stimuli.value: Smoking cue pictures depicting cigarettes and people smoking; neutral pictures depicting everyday objects and people engaged in everyday activities.
